newsitem.title: USA: US growth to slow in 2nd half 96 - Phil Fed survey.
newsitem.headline: US growth to slow in 2nd half 96 - Phil Fed survey.

text.p: Economic growth in the second half of the year is expected to decelerate from the first half's pace, according to 42 forecasters surveyed by the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia.

The forecasters expect U.S. real gross domestic product growth to register 2.5 percent in the third quarter and 2.4 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996. Year-over-year GDP growth for 1996 is seen at 2.3 percent and 1997 GDP growth is seen at 2.2 percent.

U.S. consumer price inflation is expected to advance at a 2.7 percent pace in the third quarter and by 2.9 percent in the fourth quarter. Overall, consumer prices are expected to advance by 3.2 percent in 1996 and by 3.0 percent in 1997.

The three-month Treasury bill is expected to yield, on average, 5.1 percent in the third quarter and 5.2 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996. Forecasters put the three-month T-bill rate at 5.1 percent for all of 1996 and at 5.2 percent for 1997.
Economists surveyed expect the unemployment rate to hold steady at 5.4 percent through the first quarter of 1997 and rise to 5.6 percent by the third quarter of 1997.
